how much did that block of titanium cost?

depends on the grade of titanium. CP2 (Grade2) would run about 150ish, 6Al4V (Grade5) would run about 400 or so.

That being said, it's not much good as a cutting tool, but it's a gorgeous art piece. Titanium has virtually no edge holding ability by itself. It's softer than steel by a pretty significant margin. Knifemakers that use titanium for blades will always "carbidize" the edge (use electricity to deposit tungsten carbide along the edge) to allow the carbide to do the main work of edge holding
Would that edge need to be re-carbidized over the life of the tool? How complicated/expensive is that process? I don't imagine that it would survive many sharpenings.

the process isn't bad. Most guys use old carbide drill bits or mill ends that have worn out. chuck them into a holder, apply voltage, make sparks. Video for example: Carbidizing titanium blades

The carbide is usually applied in a pretty wide band on the back of the primary bevel, so that you can resharpen without having to re-apply. That being said, it's not going to be an ideal "EDC" style blade under any circumstances. The cutting mechanics are like similar to very fine, disposable serrations. If you zoomed in really close to the edge of a carbidized blade you would see it looks like a saw blade, where the carbide deposits were raised above the surface of the titanium. As you cut, the softer titanium wears away more quickly than the carbide. Once you've sufficiently rounded off the soft titanium edge (and usually by that point broken lose or worn out the "exposed" carbide particles) you simply sharpen the knife like normal (but only on the non-carbidized side) to thin out the edge again and expose more fresh carbide.

Some of the rarer, more high end alternatives that were used in the past decade or so for non-steel blades were things like Tallonite and Stellite6k. It's the same edge concept of exposed carbide in a softer matrix material. But with Tallonite and 6k instead of the carbides being applied to the surface of the material, they are embedded throughout, with a cobalt matrix surrounding them.
